Information Retrieval is the activity of obtaining information system resources that are relevant to an information need from a collection of those resources. Searches can be based on full-text or other content-based indexing. Automated information retrieval systems are used to reduce information overload. Many universities and public libraries use IR systems to provide access to books, journals and other documents. Web search engines are the most visible IR applications.

Text summarization is the process of creating a short and coherent version of a longer document. Extractive summarization works by selecting a subset of existing words, phrases, or entire sentences in the original text to form the summary. In contrast, abstractive summarization builds an internal semantic representation and uses natural language generation techniques to create a summary that may contain words not present in the original text. TextRank is a graph-based ranking model for text processing. Graph-based ranking algorithms are essentially a way of deciding the importance of a vertex within a graph, based on global information recursively drawn from the entire graph.
